lessons.title: Eat of the good things
lessons.intro: Learn what lawful and good food means, the manners of eating from the sunnah, and the words before and after a meal.

steps.title: Food is a blessing and a test
body: Allah says: “O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah if it is [indeed] Him that you worship” (2:172). Eating well and being thankful are linked.

So food is not just fuel. Each meal is a small chance to remember who gave it. This lesson teaches what “good” means in the Qur’an, how the Prophet ﷺ taught eating, and the words to say before and after.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Lawful and good
body: The Qur’an asks for two things together: lawful (halal) and good (tayyib). “O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth [that is] lawful and good and do not follow the footsteps of Satan” (2:168). Lawful means Allah has allowed it. Good means it is clean and does you good.

Allah also says: “eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good” (5:88). The verse just before it (5:87) tells believers not to forbid the good things Allah has made lawful. So Islam does not ask us to starve or to refuse good food. It asks us to eat what is allowed, and to eat it well.
If you are unsure whether a food is halal, ask or leave it. The details of halal food are in the food guides in this app.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A boy, a dish and three rules
body: Umar ibn Abi Salamah was a boy in the Prophet’s ﷺ care. His hand used to wander all over the dish while he ate. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “O boy! Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you.” Umar said that he kept to those rules ever after (Bukhari 5376).
The Prophet ﷺ did not shout at him. He taught three small things with kindness, and a child remembered them for life.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: If you forget at the start
steps.note: The Prophet ﷺ said: when one of you eats, he should mention Allah’s name. If he forgets at the beginning, he should say these words (Abu Dawud 3767, sahih per al-Albani). The usual way to mention Allah’s name is to say Bismillah.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The Arabic is copied from the hadith cited. Saying Bismillah as the usual wording is the common practice of scholars. Please confirm.

steps.title: When you finish
steps.note: Abu Umamah said that when the table was lifted, the Prophet ﷺ used to say these words (Bukhari 5458). The Prophet ﷺ also said that Allah is pleased with a servant who says Alhamdulillah when he eats a morsel and when he drinks (Muslim 2734).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Do not waste
body: Allah says: “O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess” (7:31).
The verse allows eating and drinking, and forbids excess. It is the root of everything the next lesson says about moderation.

steps.title: Your own diet and your doctor
body: This lesson gives the general guidance of the Qur’an and sunnah. It is not medical advice. If you have a condition such as diabetes, an allergy or a heart problem, follow your doctor’s plan on what you may eat.
Allah does not charge a soul beyond its capacity (2:286). If your doctor gives you a diet, following it is not against the sunnah. It is taking care of the trust of your body.

lessons.title: The third of the stomach
lessons.intro: Learn the Prophet’s ﷺ rule of thirds, what “one intestine” means, and how to eat in moderation.

steps.title: The worst vessel
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The human being does not fill any container worse than his stomach. It is enough for the son of Adam to eat a few mouthfuls that keep his back straight. But if he must fill it, then a third for his food, a third for his drink and a third for his breath” (Tirmidhi 2380, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai; also Ibn Majah 3349, sahih per al-Albani).
He does not say that eating is bad. He says that filling the stomach is the thing to avoid, and he gives a simple rule.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Tirmidhi 2380 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai); Ibn Majah 3349 (sahih per al-Albani)

steps.title: The rule of thirds
body: First, eat only what keeps you going: a few mouthfuls to keep your back straight. This is the ideal.

If you eat more, leave your stomach in thirds: one third food, one third drink, one third air (breath). In practice, this means stopping before you feel stuffed, with room left to breathe and to drink.
The Prophet ﷺ gave a rule that is easy to remember and to follow. It is guidance, not a measuring tool.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Tirmidhi 2380 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)

steps.title: One intestine, or seven
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that the believer eats in one intestine and the unbeliever in seven (Bukhari 5393; Muslim 2060).

Ibn Umar once heard this and then refused to let a man who ate a great deal come into his house, as the report of Bukhari 5393 tells it. Scholars explain the hadith in more than one way. A common view is that it describes the believer’s moderation, and that the believer remembers Allah when he eats and stops sooner.
It is not a hadith to use against people or to judge anyone by how much they eat.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The hadith is quoted from the corpus. The explanation (a description of the believer’s moderation) is one common view among scholars, and not the only one. Please confirm.

steps.title: The Qur’an on excess
body: Allah says: “eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess” (7:31). The hadith of the thirds explains this verse in daily life.
The Qur’an also warns against the opposite mistake: forbidding what Allah made lawful (5:87). So the middle way is to eat what is good, and to stop before excess.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.text: Start with a small amount on the plate.

steps.detail: This is a common habit that helps you notice when you are full.

steps.text: Stop when you are no longer hungry, before you are full.
steps.detail: This is the meaning of leaving a third for breath.

steps.text: Drink water with the meal, or after.
steps.detail: This is the third for drink.

steps.text: Leave the table with room to spare.
steps.detail: The aim is to be light for worship and work.

steps.intro: The rule is simple. The habit takes practice.
mistakes: Eating until you cannot move.
Eating while distracted, so you do not notice you are full.
Taking more than you will finish.
steps.source: Tirmidhi 2380 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The practical tips (small plate, eat slowly) are common-sense suggestions. They are not stated in the hadith. Please confirm they may stay.

steps.title: A note on fasting and feasting
body: In Ramadan you fast from dawn to sunset, and it is easy to eat far more at night than in other months. The verse says to eat and drink and not be excessive (7:31), and that does not stop in Ramadan.
So the same rule applies at iftar and suhoor: eat what is good, and stop before you are over-full.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Applying the rule of thirds to Ramadan meals is an application, not a direct hadith. Please confirm.

steps.title: When your doctor says otherwise
body: Some people need to eat more than others, for example a growing child, a pregnant woman, someone recovering from illness or someone whose doctor has given them a plan. The rule of thirds is for a healthy adult who is tempted to over-eat.
This is not medical advice. If you are unwell, underweight or on a diet from your doctor, follow your doctor.

lessons.title: Sleep: a right of your body
lessons.intro: Learn how the Prophet ﷺ went to sleep, the words he said, and why sleep is part of a balanced life.

steps.title: Your body has a right over you
body: Abdullah ibn Amr used to pray all night and fast every day. The Prophet ﷺ warned him that his eyesight and strength would suffer, and said: “your body has a right over you, and your family has a right over you.” He told him to fast some days and not others, and to pray part of the night and then sleep (Bukhari 1153).
So sleep is not laziness. It is something your body is owed. A person who sleeps well can pray, work and be kind the next day. This lesson teaches how the Prophet ﷺ went to sleep and what he said.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Getting ready for bed
body: The Prophet ﷺ told Al-Bara ibn Azib: “When you come to your bed, make wudu as you do for prayer, then lie on your right side, and say...” and then he taught him the words in the next step. He added: make these the last words you say (Bukhari 6311).

He also said: when you go to bed, shake out your bed with the inside of your waist sheet, because you do not know what has come onto it after you left (Bukhari 6320). And he said to put out the lights, close the doors, tie the mouths of the water skins and cover the food and drink (Bukhari 6296).
These are small acts of care for yourself and your home.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The words before sleep
steps.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught this to Al-Bara. He said that if you die that night, you die on the fitrah, and to make these the last words you say. When Al-Bara repeated it back he said “your messenger” in place of “your prophet”, and the Prophet ﷺ corrected him (Bukhari 6311). Learn the words exactly.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The Arabic is copied from Bukhari 6311. The English is an explanation of the words. Please confirm.

steps.title: When you lie down
steps.note: This is the dua from Abu Huraira’s report: “In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You keep my soul, have mercy on it...” (Bukhari 6320). Sleep is a small death, and every waking is a return. You can say this dua, the one in the last step, or both.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The shortest words
steps.note: Hudhayfah said that when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed he would say these words (Bukhari 6312). If you are tired and can only say one thing, say this.

steps.title: Ayat al-Kursi
steps.note: Abu Huraira caught a thief three nights in a row. The third time, the thief said: when you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi to the end, and Allah will appoint a guard over you, and no devil will come near you till morning. The Prophet ﷺ said: “He spoke the truth, although he is an absolute liar. It was Satan” (Bukhari 2311).

steps.title: The last two verses of al-Baqarah
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will be sufficient for him (Bukhari 5009).

Scholars explain “sufficient” in more than one way: for example, that they protect him that night, or that they are enough in place of the night prayer. The hadith does not say which. Ask your imam, and recite them if you can.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The two common explanations of the word “sufficient” are given as differing views. Please confirm.

steps.title: On waking
steps.note: Hudhayfah said that when the Prophet ﷺ woke he would say these words (Bukhari 6312). They thank Allah who gave us life after the little death of sleep, and remind us of the rising.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Sleep, but do not oversleep the prayer
body: Sleep is a right, and prayer is a duty. Do not let one cancel the other. Set an alarm for Fajr and ask someone at home to wake you.
If you sleep through a prayer or forget it, pray it as soon as you remember. That is the ruling in the prayer guide.

lessons.title: Moderation in all things
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ taught about ease, small steady deeds and giving each part of life its right.

steps.title: The religion is ease
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Religion is very easy, and whoever overburdens himself in his religion will not be able to continue in that way. So do not be extremists, but try to be near to perfection, and receive the good tidings that you will be rewarded; and gain strength by worshipping in the morning, the afternoon and the last hours of the night” (Bukhari 39).
The aim is not to do less than you can. It is to do what you can keep doing.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Allah intends
body: In the verse on fasting, Allah says: “Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship” (2:185). And: “Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity” (2:286).

Ease does not mean the rules are optional. The prayers and the fast are duties. Ease means that Allah gives a way when something is truly hard: sitting to pray when you cannot stand, breaking the fast when ill, shortening the prayer on a journey.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Three men and the Prophet’s ﷺ worship
body: Three men came to the homes of the Prophet’s ﷺ wives to ask about his worship. When they were told, they felt it was little, and said: “Where are we compared to the Prophet ﷺ, whose past and future sins have been forgiven?” One said he would pray all night for ever. One said he would fast every day and never break the fast. One said he would keep away from women and never marry.

The Prophet ﷺ came and said: “Are you the ones who said such and such? By Allah, I am more submissive to Allah and more afraid of Him than you. Yet I fast and I break my fast, I sleep, and I also marry women. Whoever does not follow my sunnah is not from me” (Bukhari 5063).
He did not tell them to worship less. He told them to worship in the way he did, which includes rest and a normal life.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Small and regular
body: Aisha reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do good deeds properly, sincerely and moderately, and know that your deeds will not make you enter Paradise, and that the most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular and constant, even if it is little” (Bukhari 6464).
A short prayer or a page of Qur’an every day is better than a great effort once and then nothing.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Two blessings many people lose
body: Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There are two blessings that many people lose out on: health and free time” (Bukhari 6412).
So health is a blessing to use, and free time is a blessing to use well. Looking after your health is not wasted time. It is looking after a blessing from Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Moderation is not an excuse
body: Moderation never means skipping what is obligatory. A person cannot say “religion is ease” and then miss the prayer. The ease is inside the rules, and not a way around them.
If you are unsure whether you are being easy on yourself or neglecting a duty, ask a teacher you trust.
steps.label: [Interpretive]

lessons.title: The Prophet’s own ruqyah
lessons.intro: Learn the ruqyah of the Prophet ﷺ: the dua for pain, the dua for the sick, the surahs of refuge and what makes a ruqyah correct.

steps.title: The Qur’an as healing
body: Allah says: “And We send down of the Qur’an that which is healing and mercy for the believers” (17:82). And: “O mankind, there has to come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers” (10:57).

Ruqyah (ruqya) is reciting the Qur’an and the duas of the Prophet ﷺ over yourself or another person, asking Allah for healing and protection. It is a sunnah. It comes with trust that the cure is from Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Uthman and the pain in his body
body: Uthman ibn Abi al-As complained to the Prophet ﷺ of a pain he had felt in his body ever since he became Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: put your hand on the place where you feel pain in your body, say Bismillah three times, and say seven times the words in the next step (Muslim 2202).
The cure he gave was simple: a hand, the name of Allah, and a dua. No special place, no special person.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The words for pain
steps.note: Say Bismillah three times with your hand on the place of the pain, then say this seven times (Muslim 2202). It means: I seek refuge with Allah and with His power from the evil of what I find and what I fear.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The dua the Prophet ﷺ made for the sick
steps.note: Aisha said that when the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick person, or one was brought to him, he would say these words (Bukhari 5675). You can say them for anyone who is ill, and for yourself.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The two surahs of refuge
body: Aisha said that whenever the Prophet ﷺ fell ill, he would recite the two surahs of refuge (al-Falaq and an-Nas), blow lightly over himself and wipe his hands over his body. In his last illness she did this for him, as he used to do (Bukhari 4439).
The surahs begin: “I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak” (113:1) and “I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind” (114:1).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Hear the first ayah of al-Falaq
The Fatihah as ruqyah
body: Some Companions stayed with a tribe who would not host them. The tribe’s chief was bitten by a snake or stung by a scorpion, and they asked if the Companions had a ruqyah. One of them recited Surat al-Fatihah over him and the chief was cured. The Companions would not accept the flock of sheep they were offered until they asked the Prophet ﷺ.
He smiled and said: “How did you know that it is a ruqyah? Take it, and give me a share with you” (Bukhari 5736).
It shows that the Fatihah can be recited as ruqyah, and that taking payment for it was allowed in that case.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The ruling on taking payment for ruqyah differs among the schools, and this step does not give it. Please add the school positions if they are to be included.

steps.title: What makes a ruqyah correct
body: Auf ibn Malik said they used to do incantations in the days before Islam and asked the Prophet ﷺ about them. He said: show me your incantations, and there is no harm in an incantation that does not contain shirk (Muslim 2200).

So a ruqyah is correct when it uses the Qur’an and the duas of the Prophet ﷺ, or other words that are clear and contain no shirk. It must not call on anyone but Allah, and not use words you do not understand. And it must be done with the belief that Allah alone heals.
Ruqyah is not a way to harm someone or to look for the unseen.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: Muslim 2200 gives only the rule of no shirk. The conditions that the words be understood and that Allah alone heals are the usual conditions listed by scholars. Please confirm.

steps.title: Ruqyah and the doctor
body: Ruqyah does not replace the doctor. If you are in pain, see a doctor, and use the ruqyah too. The next lessons show the Prophet ﷺ told us to seek treatment.
This is not medical advice. If symptoms are serious or last, please go to a doctor.

lessons.title: The evil eye: real, and curable
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ taught about the evil eye, how to protect yourself and your family, and what to do if it happens.

steps.title: The evil eye is real
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The effect of the evil eye is real” (Bukhari 5740). In Muslim 2188, Ibn Abbas reported that he said it is real, and that if anything could race ahead of the divine decree, it would be the evil eye.
Allah also tells us to seek refuge from “the evil of an envier when he envies” (113:5). The eye is linked to envy, or to a look of admiration that does not mention Allah.
We believe it is real. We do not fear it, and we do not see it behind every misfortune.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Sahl ibn Hunayf
body: Amir ibn Rabi’ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing, and said: “I have never seen skin like this.” Sahl fell to the ground at once. He was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, who asked: “Whom do you accuse?” They said: Amir ibn Rabi’ah.

The Prophet ﷺ said: “Why would any of you kill his brother? If one of you sees something that he likes in his brother, let him pray for blessing for him.” Then he called for water, told Amir to make wudu, and had the water poured over Sahl (Ibn Majah 3509, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
Notice that Amir did not mean harm. The eye can come from admiration with no ill will.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Ibn Majah 3509 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)

steps.title: When you admire something
body: The Prophet ﷺ taught to pray for blessing for what you admire, and to say what Allah wills. Allah teaches in a story: “Why did you, when you entered your garden, not say, ‘What Allah willed [has occurred]; there is no power except in Allah’?” (18:39).
So when you admire a child, a house or a person, say: ma sha Allah, la quwwata illa billah, and ask Allah to bless it. This keeps the admiration from turning into harm.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Ibn Majah 3509 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai); Qur’an 18:39
steps.review: The phrase “ma sha Allah, la quwwata illa billah” is taken from 18:39 and is the usual thing to say. It is not given as the Prophet’s ﷺ own wording in the hadith of Sahl. Please confirm.

steps.title: The refuge for children
steps.note: Ibn Abbas said that the Prophet ﷺ used to seek Allah’s refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn with these words, and said that their forefather Ibrahim used to seek refuge with them for Ismail and Ishaq (Bukhari 3371). Parents can say them over their children.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The cure
body: In the story above, the Prophet ﷺ had Amir make wudu and then had the water poured over Sahl. In Muslim 2188 he also said: “if you are asked to wash, then wash.” So if someone was affected by your look and asks you to wash, you should do it.
Scholars describe exactly how the washing is done in more than one way. If this ever happens to you, ask a scholar to guide you on the steps.
Along with this, the cures from the last lesson apply: ruqyah, the surahs of refuge and the dua for the sick.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Ibn Majah 3509 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai); Muslim 2188
steps.review: The details of how the washing is done differ among scholars and have not been given. Please confirm that sending the learner to a scholar is acceptable.

steps.title: Do not accuse, and do not panic
body: The Prophet ﷺ asked who they accused, but did not punish Amir. He said that a brother should not “kill” his brother by his look. He taught a cure and a manner, not a hunt for the guilty.
So do not accuse a person of casting the evil eye without proof. And do not blame every illness or bad day on the eye. Most illness has a medical cause and needs a doctor.

lessons.title: Medicine and faith together
lessons.intro: Learn that the Prophet ﷺ told us to seek treatment, how trust in Allah and medicine go together, and what to say to the sick.

steps.title: Every disease has a treatment
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “There is no disease that Allah has created, except that He also created its treatment” (Bukhari 5678). In Muslim 2204, Jabir reported that he said there is a remedy for every illness, and when the right remedy is applied to the disease, it is cured by the permission of Allah.
So we do not choose between faith and medicine. Allah made the illness, Allah made the cure, and Allah heals through it.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Seek treatment
body: Some Bedouins asked the Prophet ﷺ: “Messenger of Allah, shall we seek treatment?” He said: “Yes, servants of Allah, seek treatment. Allah has not made a disease without making a cure for it, except one disease.” They asked what it was and he said: “Old age” (Tirmidhi 2038, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai; Abu Dawud 3855, sahih per al-Albani).
So going to the doctor and taking the medicine is part of the sunnah. It is not a lack of trust in Allah.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Tirmidhi 2038 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai); Abu Dawud 3855 (sahih per al-Albani)

steps.title: Tie the camel, then trust
body: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ: “Shall I tie my camel and trust in Allah, or leave it loose and trust in Allah?” He said: “Tie it, and trust in Allah” (Tirmidhi 2517, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
Trust in Allah (tawakkul) is not doing nothing. You do what you can, and then you rely on Allah for the result. Medicine is part of what you do.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Tirmidhi 2517 (hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)

steps.title: It is He who cures me
body: The prophet Ibrahim said: “And when I am ill, it is He who cures me” (26:80). He said “when I am ill”, and “He cures”. The doctor and the medicine are the means, and the cure is from Allah.
This is why Muslims say Alhamdulillah when they recover, and thank the doctor too.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What to say to the sick
steps.note: When the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick person, he used to say these words. Once he said them to a bedouin who answered back that it was a fever that would send him to the grave. The Prophet ﷺ said, “Then so be it” (Bukhari 3616). It is a lesson to speak good words to the sick.

steps.title: Protecting others
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “If you hear of an outbreak of plague in a land, do not enter it. If it breaks out in a place while you are in it, do not leave that place” (Bukhari 5728).

Scholars use this hadith as a basis for protecting people from contagious disease. Today, doctors and health authorities give guidance for each outbreak. Follow their advice on staying home, hygiene and vaccination as it applies to you.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Applying the hadith to today’s public health guidance is the usual understanding of scholars. Please confirm and check the wording about vaccination.

steps.intro: There is no conflict between them.

lessons.title: The sound heart
lessons.intro: Learn why the sound heart is what counts, the hadith of the piece of flesh, and a dua and a daily check for a steady heart.

steps.title: The only thing that will help
body: Allah describes a day when “there will not benefit [anyone] wealth or children, but only one who comes to Allah with a sound heart” (26:88-89).
The lessons so far were about the body: food, sleep, medicine. This lesson is about the part that matters most on that day: the heart.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The piece of flesh
body: An-Nu’man ibn Bashir heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Beware! There is a piece of flesh in the body. If it is good, the whole body is good. If it is spoilt, the whole body is spoilt. And that is the heart” (Bukhari 52).
In the Qur’an and the hadith, “the heart” is where a person believes, intends, loves and fears. A healthy heart shows in a person’s deeds, and a sick heart shows in them too.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Allah looks at
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah does not look at your faces and your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds” (Muslim 2564).
This does not mean looks and health do not matter. It means they are not what we are judged by.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The one who purifies it
body: Allah swears by the soul and then says: “He has succeeded who purifies it, And he has failed who instills it [with corruption]” (91:9-10). And: “He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself and mentions the name of his Lord and prays” (87:14-15).
Purifying the heart (tazkiyah) is therefore a lifelong task, and the Qur’an links it to remembering Allah and to prayer.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A dua for a steady heart
steps.note: Abdullah ibn Amr heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The hearts of all the children of Adam are between two fingers of the Merciful, like one heart. He turns it wherever He wills.” Then the Prophet ﷺ said these words (Muslim 2655).
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The Arabic is copied from Muslim 2655. The words “two fingers of the Merciful” are quoted from the hadith. We do not give them a meaning. Please confirm how the hadith should be explained to a beginner.

steps.title: A dua from the Qur’an
body: The believers in the Qur’an say: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower” (3:8).
This is a verse you can make your own dua. It asks for what the hadith above asks for: a heart that stays steady.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Signs that the heart needs care
body: Allah says of the hypocrites, “In their hearts is disease” (2:10). Scholars take this as a warning that a heart can be sick. Later lessons in this Academy cover the main diseases: showing off, envy, pride, despair and anger.

A person can tell when the heart is unwell: prayer feels heavy, the Qur’an means nothing, and sins feel small. These are not tests of faith that anyone else can mark. They are signs for you to turn back to Allah.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The signs listed are common teaching and are not a hadith. Please confirm.

steps.title: If your heart is heavy
body: A heavy heart is not always a spiritual problem. If you are sad, anxious or numb for weeks, talk to a doctor or someone you trust, as well as turning to Allah. Seeking help is not a lack of faith.
If you are in danger or thinking of harming yourself, use the Need help now button in this app.

lessons.title: Dhikr: food for the heart
lessons.intro: Learn why remembering Allah gives the heart rest, two light words of dhikr and how to keep a small daily habit.

steps.title: Hearts find rest
body: Allah says of the believers: “those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured” (13:28).
Dhikr is remembering Allah: with the tongue, saying words of praise; with the heart, being aware of Him; and with the limbs, obeying Him. This lesson is about the words of dhikr.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: I will remember you
body: Allah says: “So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me” (2:152).

In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: “I am with My servant when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself. If he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better gathering” (Bukhari 7405; Muslim 2675).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The living and the dead
body: Abu Musa reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The example of the one who remembers his Lord and the one who does not is like the living and the dead” (Bukhari 6407).
A heart without dhikr does not stop all at once. It becomes numb. Dhikr is its food.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Two light words
steps.note: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Two words that are light on the tongue, heavy in the balance and dear to the Merciful: Subhan Allah al-Azim, Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi” (Bukhari 6406). They take a few seconds to say.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The reward of tasbih
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever says Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi one hundred times a day, his sins are forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea” (Bukhari 6405).
Dhikr is a sunnah and a mercy. It does not replace the prayer or repentance, and does not give permission to sin.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The note that dhikr does not replace the obligatory acts is the standard understanding of the scholars of hadith. Please confirm.

steps.title: In every state
body: Allah describes people of understanding as people who “remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth” (3:191).
Dhikr does not need a special place. You can do it walking, sitting in a bus, cooking or lying in bed. That is why it is the food of the heart: you can eat it all day.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Small and regular
body: The most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular, even if it is little (Bukhari 6464). Choose a small amount of dhikr you can keep every day. Even a hundred times of Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi takes only a few minutes.
Many people find it easier to attach dhikr to something they already do: after prayer, on the way to work, or before sleep.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The advice to attach dhikr to existing habits is practical guidance and not a hadith. Please confirm.
